findings.detail: PASS: the record conservatively treats whole-tree archive creation and extraction as protected-byte access even though no protected content was printed, parsed, or used.

PASS subject to the stated review limitations: the record names the exact temporary root, records its approved deletion, states that verification stopped before commands ran inside the extracted tree, and forbids scientific use of archived bytes.
PASS: the record grants no promotion or execution authority, leaves V4 permanently ineligible for G8, and AGENTS.md continues to make every legacy sealed role inaccessible.

PASS as a narrow procedural guard: it covers git archive, worktree export, checkout copies, source packages, and equivalent clean-tree materialization while legacy sealed blobs remain tracked. It is not an operating-system access-control boundary.

BLOCK: AGENTS.md currently permits only paths in the 72-path committed source-closure manifest, while the incident record requires those paths plus separately reviewed checker and synthetic-test files; the governing closure also has nine explicit checker, guard, and synthetic-test paths. The current wording either forbids required verification files or invites an undocumented exception.
findings.required_agents_wording: Clean source verification must export only (a) the 72 validated paths in the committed source-closure manifest and (b) the nine checker, guard, and synthetic-test paths explicitly enumerated and SHA-256-bound in the governing source-closure review receipt; every exported path must be validated against its binding before copying.
findings.required_incident_wording: Clean source certification must construct a source-only snapshot from exactly the 72 paths bound by the committed closure manifest plus the nine checker, guard, and synthetic-test paths explicitly enumerated and SHA-256-bound in the governing source-closure review receipt.

limitations: This source-only review did not inspect Git object membership, protected paths, sealed bytes, config or custody roots, the archive, the extracted tree, the deleted temporary root, or retained command logs.

Claims about exact archived membership, deletion, absence of downstream protected-byte use, and the 72-plus-9 closure inventory are assessed as documented custody assertions rather than independently re-executed facts.
The proposed wording remains procedural defense in depth; a safe exporter must enforce the exact allowlist and hashes fail-closed.
